content:
The image shows a split soybean stem held in hand. Key observations:

- Stem is split lengthwise, exposing the internal pith
- The pith is **white** (not brown)
- There is some gray/bluish discoloration along the vascular tissue and inner stem walls
- The outer stem tissue appears bleached/tan, consistent with a mature/dead plant
- No white fluffy mold, no black sclerotia visible
- The internal discoloration is grayish-brown in the vascular/woody tissue, while the pith remains white

The white pith is the critical diagnostic feature here. Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS) is explicitly distinguished from Brown Stem Rot by having **white pith** when stems are cut, while BSR causes brown pith. The grayish discoloration in the woody tissue of the stem is consistent with SDS description: "the woody tissue of the taproot is discolored light gray to brown." The white pith eliminates Brown Stem Rot.
